primitives.name: Presentation Bias Model
primitives.verbatim_quote: US 8,938,463 B1 MODIFYING SEARCH RESULT RANKING BASED ON IMPLICIT USER FEEDBACK AND A MODEL OF PRESENTATION BIAS BACKGROUND The present disclosure relates to ranking of search results.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'B': 'dimensionless presentation bias factor', 'F': 'feature vector of user context', 'Q': 'query identifier'}
primitives.assumptions: Presentation bias is modeled as a deterministic function of user context features F and query Q.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When F is insufficiently informative or Q is ambiguous, B becomes undefined.

layer2.mapping: Maps contextual features to a probabilistic adjustment of relevance scores in GSI's Bayesian framework.
layer2.telemetry: Click-through rate deviation from expected baseline.

primitives.name: Implicit User Feedback Signal
primitives.verbatim_quote: For example, user reactions to particular search results or search result lists may be gauged, so that results on which users often click will receive a higher ranking.
primitives.assumptions: User clicks are proxies for relevance; C is binary.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When U is sparse or C is noisy, signal-to-noise ratio degrades.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to GSI's relevance estimation kernel, where U maps to R via empirical Bayes.
layer2.telemetry: Normalized click frequency per document across queries.

primitives.name: Link-Based Relevance Inference
primitives.verbatim_quote: For example, search results can have an elevated importance, or inferred relevance, if a number of other search results link to them.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'L': 'link graph adjacency matrix', 'S': 'source document set', 'T': 'target document set', 'R_{in}(d)': 'inbound relevance score of document d'}
primitives.assumptions: Relevance propagates through hyperlinks; L is static or slowly evolving.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When L is sparse or contains spam links, R_{in} becomes unreliable.

layer2.mapping: Derives document relevance in GSE via iterative propagation on L, akin to PageRank.
layer2.telemetry: PageRank-like convergence metrics for document rank stability.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that search ranking integrates explicit and implicit signals into a unified probabilistic framework. Presentation bias B(Q,F) modifies raw relevance estimates, while implicit feedback U provides empirical validation. Link-based inference R_in(d) acts as a secondary confirmation layer. These components interlock: B adjusts how relevance is perceived, U refines estimates, and L offers structural consistency. The failure mode occurs when one component fails—e.g., if F is missing, B collapses; if U is absent, feedback loop breaks; if L is corrupted, trust in structure erodes. Dualities emerge between user behavior and structural properties, with each modality offering orthogonal yet complementary views of relevance. The system’s robustness depends on cross-validation among these modalities.
